newsitem.title: USA: Fore, Hewlett-Packard in ATM pact.
newsitem.headline: Fore, Hewlett-Packard in ATM pact.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co and Fore Systems Inc said Monday they had agreed to jointly develop a next-generation high-speed multimedia network switching system.
The companies said they plan to combine their stackable Ethernet and Asynchronous Transfer Mode technologies to develop an ATM module for HP's AdvanceStack Switch 2000.

They said the AdvanceStack Switch 2000 ATM module (HP J3246A) will be priced at $8,999 and is expected to be available later this year through HP's worldwide network of authorized computer dealers, resellers and distributors.
Ethernet is the standard method for laying out computer local area networks. ATM is a new method for building networks to handle high-speed voice and video transmissions.

The HP/Fore ATM system would allow users to integrate transitional Ethernet workgroup technologies called 10Base-T, 100Base-T, 100VG-AnyLAN and FDDI -- with high-capacity ATM backbone systems, the companies said.

The companies said HP's AdvanceStack Switch 2000 with an ATM uplink module is expected to improve the performance of existing networks while providing a smooth migration path to future high-speed networks and to allow transitional Ethernet, FDDI and 100 VG networks to connect to ATM-based systems.
The partners said their joint development effort will focus on delivering a tight integration of LAN Ethernet technologies into an ATM infrastructure.
